data.note: buglane27: fix B93e00ef048 foreign-launch guard false-refuses run_cli launches from the linked worktree; widen globs to the guard + test helper

evidence.note: Claim: run_cli's `python -m ddflow` subprocess is refused `imported from the linked worktree` because it imports ddflow from the linked worktree while the launcher stands inside the checkout family, which the guard treats as a cross-lane run. Probe (python one-liner invoking guard_foreign_launch with PYTHONPATH=<worktree>): cwd=primary -> guard_exit 1 ('imported from the linked worktree'); cwd=/tmp sandbox (outside family) -> guard_exit 0. The fix anchors run_cli's subprocess cwd to the repo under test (outside the family), the explicit external launch the guard permits (matches test_an_explicit_pythonpath_launch_from_an_unrelated_repository_is_allowed). VERDICT CONFIRMED.

Test-only change in tests/_cli_helpers.py (r-adapters n/a; no new external dependency). Regression test added to tests/test_lease_keep_long_commands.py, the file the bug names. run_cli docstring cites B93e00ef048. No config/CLI/MCP surface change, so r-feature-four-ways n/a.

tests/_cli_helpers.py run_cli sets cwd=str(repo) (subprocess now runs in the repository under test). Regression test test_run_cli_anchors_the_subprocess_in_the_repository_under_test asserts seen['cwd']==str(repo).
.venv/bin/ruff check tests/_cli_helpers.py tests/test_lease_keep_long_commands.py -> All checks passed; ruff format --check -> 2 files already formatted.

chunk_findings.detail: The change sets `cwd=str(repo)` without making `repo` absolute, so relative repository paths now change meaning. `subprocess.run` resolves a relative `cwd` against the parent process’s cwd, while the child process receives `--repo <relative>` and resolves that argument against its new cwd. For example, if the test process cwd is `/tmp/tests` and `repo=Path("hub")`, the old behavior launched the CLI with `--repo hub` in `/tmp/tests`, targeting `/tmp/tests/hub`; the new behavior launches with cwd `/tmp/tests/hub`, so the child resolves `hub` as `/tmp/tests/hub/hub`. If that directory does not exist the CLI fails before it can initialize or operate; if it exists, the test operates on the wrong repository. The added regression test does not catch this because it only asserts that the monkeypatched `subprocess.run` saw `cwd == str(repo)`, not that the path is absolute or that the CLI actually targeted the intended repository.
chunk_findings.title: tests/_cli_helpers.py:39 (`run_cli` subprocess `cwd`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new `cwd=str(root)` changes which `ddflow` package the subprocess imports, because `python -m` puts the process cwd ahead of `PYTHONPATH` on `sys.path`. If `repo` is another checkout/worktree of this project (for example `/wt` containing a `ddflow/` package) while `_cli_helpers.py` lives in `/main`, then `run_cli(Path("/wt"), "status")` now launches `python -m ddflow` with cwd `/wt`, so the child imports `/wt/ddflow` instead of the `/main/ddflow` selected by `PYTHONPATH`. A stale linked worktree can therefore make tests fail, or a bug fixed in the test tree can be masked because the subprocess silently runs the repo’s code rather than the code under test.

chunk_findings.detail: The new upgrade note claims that tighten-only layering lets “a company floor keep bugs_first first,” but the new `order_pin` documentation says the opposite: pinned keys from a more senior layer lead ahead of lower-layer pins, so a company pin for `bugs_first` is not necessarily first. For example, with a company/lower layer setting `order_pin = ["bugs_first"]` and a more senior layer setting `order_pin = ["critical_path"]`, the effective order begins with `critical_path`, not `bugs_first`. The template’s stated guarantee is therefore false and contradicts the documented contract.

chunk_findings.detail: The added `order` knob documents its default as `[recover_first, bugs_first, unphased_first, priority, id]`, while the adjacent `optimizer` knob in the same config section still documents `greedy-v1` as using “the order keys bugs first, priority, id.” This change therefore introduces two mutually inconsistent descriptions of the default scheduler order. A user who follows the optimizer documentation and sets `schedule.order = ["bugs_first", "priority", "id"]` to preserve what that knob says is the default will, if the new `order` knob’s documented default is actually installed, silently lose the `recover_first` and `unphased_first` keys.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/schedule.py:order

chunk_findings.detail: The new upgrade note’s `why` field states that `order_pin` is “tighten-only across layers, so a company floor can keep `bugs_first` first,” but the rewritten contract in `docs/guide/parallelism.md:313` says the opposite: a layer’s keys lead, and a lower company pin is kept “not necessarily first if a more-senior layer pins another key.” For example, if a company config sets `schedule.order_pin = ["bugs_first"]` and a user/local layer above it sets `schedule.order_pin = ["critical_path"]`, the effective order begins with `critical_path`, then `bugs_first`. The template therefore advertises a guarantee that the documented semantics do not provide.

data.body: Generalize the ad-hoc controller cron into a shipped ddflow standard: ddflow dispatch already emits per-tick advice ("steer RESUME lane-X; refill; recover"). Wire that into session-init (ddflow onboard / brief) and into the lane-end event so the coordinator (ANY harness: kilo/claude/copilot) is TOLD to run ddflow dispatch and ACT on its RESUME/refill/recover advice to keep lanes full and phases driving to exhaustion — respecting DAG: dependent/overlapping-glob items sequential in the SAME lane, independent items parallel across lanes. This closes the gap where lanes end and idly wait for an operator to say resume. Tests first.
data.title: Dispatch-driven self-management: the coordinator runs ddflow dispatch at session-init and each lane-end, acting on RESUME/refill/recover to exhaustion
